minutes.headline: School and town budgets face deep cuts unless voters pass a tier-1 or tier-2 override in May
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee held a joint public hearing on the FY27 school and town budgets, hearing detailed presentations on a "balanced" (level-funded) budget with drastic staffing and program cuts (including eliminated sports, reduced athletic training, and larger class sizes) versus two override scenarios (tier 1 and tier 2) that would restore and add positions across schools, police, fire, DPW, library, and recreation. No votes were taken on the budget, override, or warrant articles at this meeting; the committee closed the public hearing, reviewed draft warrant articles, and scheduled an additional virtual meeting for April 6th to vote on articles and finalize its report before the town meeting warrant deadline.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee closed its public hearing on the FY27 school and town budgets without voting on the budget, an override, or any warrant article.

The superintendent laid out a level-funded budget with cuts to teaching positions, music, and athletics, against two override scenarios that would restore and add staff across schools, police, fire, DPW, and the library.
Draft warrant articles, including the override article itself, were walked through but not voted on.
The committee scheduled an additional virtual meeting for April 6 to vote on the warrant articles and finalize its report before the town meeting deadline.

why_it_matters: Whether voters pass a tier-1 or tier-2 override in May decides whether class sizes rise and positions such as teachers, a custodian, and an occupational therapy assistant go unfilled.
The warrant articles still being drafted will set exactly what residents are asked to vote on at town meeting and on the override ballot.
Town departments including police, fire, DPW, and the library face the same level-funded-versus-override choice as the schools.
watch_next: April 6 virtual Finance Committee meeting: vote on warrant articles and the committee's report
May 2 town meeting warrant vote and May 16 override ballot vote

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the roll-call votes and on most dollar figures that both sides actually stated — mainly differing where ours mangled digit-grouping in numbers read off slides (our captions systematically drop internal commas/decimals, e.g. "$269,48.83" for "$269,048.83").
